lines: “洛晖，货呢？”
黑市掮客老葛把一只裂口木箱拍在修补台上，箱里滚出三枚断齿齿轮，两截烧焦铜线，半片星纹薄板。
“你昨晚拿走我一枚报废罗盘，说天亮前修好。现在太阳都快下班了，罗盘呢？”
洛晖蹲在台边，嘴里叼着一枚银钉，左手按住罗盘外壳，右手用细铜针挑开星纹槽里的黑灰。
“老葛，太阳下班还领薪水，我修你这破玩意儿只收两个铜角。你催得这么理直气壮，脸皮也该拿去镶甲，防御肯定比铁卫盾牌高。”
老葛伸手去抓罗盘：“少贫。废墟镇三条街都知道你只会捡废铁。”
洛晖抬脚勾住木箱边缘，箱盖啪地弹起，挡住老葛的手。他吐掉银钉，铜针往星纹槽里一压。
咔嗒。
罗盘中央裂开的晶片亮起一圈浅蓝光，指针先抽搐两下，接着稳稳指向北侧旧矿坑。
老葛伸出的手停在半空。
洛晖把罗盘推过去：“废铁修好了。您老人家要不要给它磕一个？毕竟它刚从坟里爬出来，仪式感得有。”
老葛抓起罗盘，低头看指针，脸上的肉抖了一下。
“北边？旧矿坑封了十年，那里只有塌洞、老鼠、巡夜铁卫。罗盘坏了吧？”
“你刚才骂我只会捡废铁，现在又怀疑废铁指路。老葛，你这客户体验挺分裂。”
洛晖把台下旧皮甲拽出来套上，顺手摸过银扣短披风，披风边角磨得发白，扣子倒擦得很亮。
老葛压低脖子，往门外扫了一圈：“今晚有人在收矿坑蓝火残片。一片三枚银轮。你要真能找着，咱们五五分。”
洛晖伸出两根手指。
老葛瞪他。
“三七。”洛晖拿起罗盘，“我七，你三。你负责闭嘴，任务最重，值得三成。”
“你小子迟早被铁卫吊在镇口。”
“那我也先把绳子卖了。”
修补铺外，贫民区的街巷铺着碎石，污水顺着星纹排水槽往低处流。屋顶架着废弃蒸汽管，管壁有裂缝，白汽一阵一阵往外喷。远处钟塔缺了半边，塔顶炼金灯忽明忽暗，照出矿坑方向一片低矮废墙。
罗盘指针开始发颤。
洛晖低头，胸口贴着皮肤的铜星坠突然发烫。他伸手按住坠子，指腹碰到坠面凹凸不平的刻线。
十年前，同样的蓝火夜，洛沉蹲在门槛前，把这枚铜星坠挂到他脖子上。
那时屋外铁靴踏过泥水，矿坑方向有蓝火冲起。洛沉替他把衣领拉高，只留下一句话。
“别让它离开你。”
门合上后，洛沉再没回来。
洛晖把铜星坠塞进衣领里，抬手弹了弹罗盘：“行，老爹留下的老古董都发烫了。三枚银轮也发烫。今晚不去，明天得后悔到棺材板里。”
老葛从柜台底下摸出一张灰纸：“旧矿坑外圈有废墟帮的人守着，铁卫也巡夜。你别从正门钻，南侧排气渠还能进。”
洛晖接过灰纸，扫了一眼路线，塞进袖口。
“老葛，你终于干了件掮客该干的事。”
“少废话。拿到残片先交给我。”
洛晖走到门口，回头冲他一抬下巴：“要是我没回来，罗盘算我送你。记得给我立块牌子，写‘废铁之王洛晖，死于客户太抠’。”
老葛抓起螺母砸过去。
洛晖侧身避开，螺母砸在门框上，哐当落地。他弯腰捡起，塞进口袋。
“谢了，路上防身。”
贫民区往北，街巷越走越窄。洛晖踩着墙边凸起的砖块翻上废管，避开下方巡夜帮派的篝火。两名废墟帮打手蹲在铁桶旁喝劣酒，腰间挂着短刀，脚边堆着抢来的铜线。
“矿坑那边又冒蓝火了。”
“管它。铁卫今晚查得紧，别过去送命。”
洛晖趴在管道上方，慢慢挪过破口。铜星坠烫得更狠，贴在胸口，烫出一圈红印。他咬住袖口，把疼压下去。
旧矿坑外围竖着半塌的铁门，门上挂着皇城铁卫团的旧封条。封条被风吹得翻卷，黑字还清楚：魔法复兴历三零七年，旧矿坑永久封禁。
洛晖盯着“三零七年”四个字，手指在封条边缘停了一下。
content_en:
"Luo Hui, where is the goods?"
Black market broker Lao Ge slapped a cracked wooden box on the repair table. Three broken gears, two pieces of burnt copper wire, and half a star pattern sheet rolled out of the box.
"You took a scrapped compass from me last night and said it would be repaired before dawn. The sun is about to go off work now, where is the compass?"
Luo Hui squatted by the stage, holding a silver nail in his mouth, holding the compass shell with his left hand, and using a thin copper needle with his right hand to pick up the black ash in the star pattern groove.
"Old Ge, Taiyang still gets paid after get off work, but I only charge you two copper horns to repair this broken thing of yours. You are so arrogant and confident, you should wear armor for your face. The defense must be higher than the Iron Guard shield."
Lao Ge reached out to grab the compass: "Young poor man. Everyone in the three streets of Ruinian Town knows that you can only pick up scrap metal."
Luo Hui raised his foot and hooked the edge of the wooden box. The lid of the box popped up, blocking Lao Ge's hand. He spit out the silver nail and pressed the copper needle into the star pattern groove.
Click.
The cracked chip in the center of the compass lit up with a circle of light blue light. The pointer twitched twice first, and then pointed steadily to the old mine on the north side.
Lao Ge's outstretched hand stopped in mid-air.
Luo Hui pushed the compass over: "The scrap iron has been repaired. Would you like to give it a kowtow? After all, it just climbed out of the grave, so it has a sense of ceremony."
Lao Ge grabbed the compass, looked down at the pointer, and the flesh on his face trembled.
"North? The old mine has been closed for ten years. There are only caves, rats, and night watch guards there. Is the compass broken?"
"You just scolded me for only picking up scrap metal, and now you doubt that scrap metal will guide you. Lao Ge, your customer experience is quite divided."
Luo Hui pulled out the old leather armor from the audience and put it on, then touched the silver-buttoned short cloak. The corners of the cloak were worn white, but the buttons were polished brightly.
Lao Ge lowered his neck and glanced around the door: "Tonight someone is collecting the blue fire fragments from the mine. There are three silver wheels in each piece. If you can really find it, we will give you 50-50."
Luo Hui stretched out two fingers.
Lao Ge glared at him.
"Thirty-seven." Luo Hui picked up the compass, "I am seven, you are three. You are responsible for shutting up. The task is the heaviest and it is worth 30%."
"Sooner or later, your kid will be hung at the entrance of the town by the iron guards."
"Then I'll sell the rope first."
Outside the repair shop, the streets of the slums were paved with gravel, and sewage flowed downwards along the star-patterned drainage channels. There were abandoned steam pipes on the roof. There were cracks in the pipe walls, and white steam was spraying out. In the distance, half of the clock tower was missing, and the alchemy lamp on the top of the tower flickered on and off, illuminating a low ruined wall in the direction of the mine.
The compass needle began to tremble.
Luo Hui lowered his head, and the copper star pendant against his skin suddenly became hot. He stretched out his hand to hold the pendant, and his fingertips touched the uneven carved lines on the pendant's surface.
Ten years ago, on the same blue fire night, Luo Chen squatted in front of the threshold and hung this bronze star pendant around his neck.
At that time, iron boots stepped on the muddy water outside the house, and blue fire shot up in the direction of the mine. Luo Chen pulled up his collar for him and left only one sentence.
"Don't let it get away from you."
After the door closed, Luo Chen never came back.
Luo Hui stuffed the copper star pendant into his collar, raised his hand and flicked the compass: "Okay, the old antiques left behind by dad are hot. The three silver wheels are also hot. If you don't go tonight, you will regret it in the coffin board tomorrow."
Lao Ge took out a piece of gray paper from under the counter and said: "There are people from the Ruin Gang guarding the outer perimeter of the old mine, and the iron guards are also on watch at night. Don't go through the front entrance, the south side exhaust canal can still be entered."
Luo Hui took the gray paper, glanced at the route, and stuffed it into his cuffs.
"Lao Ge, you finally did something a broker should do."
"Stop talking nonsense. Get the remaining pieces and give them to me first."
Luo Hui walked to the door, turned around and raised his chin at him: "If I don't come back, Luo Pan plans to send you off. Remember to put up a sign for me and write 'Luo Hui, the King of Scrap Iron, died because of being too picky about his customers'."
Lao Ge grabbed the nut and smashed it.
Luo Hui turned sideways to avoid it, and the nut hit the door frame and landed with a clang. He bent down to pick it up and stuffed it into his pocket.
"Thanks, please protect yourself on the road."
To the north of the slums, the streets become narrower and narrower. Luo Hui stepped on the raised bricks on the wall and climbed up the waste pipe to avoid the bonfire of the night watch gang below. Two Ruin Gang thugs were squatting next to a metal barrel drinking bad wine, with short knives hanging on their waists and looted copper wires piled at their feet.
"There's blue fire coming out of the mine again."
"Never mind it. The Iron Guard will check closely tonight, don't go there and die."
Luo Hui lay on top of the pipe and slowly moved over the breach. The copper star pendant was burned even more fiercely, sticking to the chest and leaving a red mark. He bit his cuff to suppress the pain.
A half-collapsed iron gate stood outside the old mine, and the old seal of the Imperial City Iron Guard hung on the gate. The seal was blown by the wind, and the black words were still clear: Magic Revival Calendar 307, the old mine is permanently closed.
Luo Hui stared at the words "Three Years and Seven Years" and paused with his fingers on the edge of the seal.
